items.title: AI and your job: Threat or opportunity?
items.summary:
MOBILE, Ala. (WALA) - Artificial intelligence is becoming a bigger part of everyday life, raising questions about what the technology could mean for workers and their jobs.

Some economists believe AI poses a particular threat to entry-level and repetitive work, including call center, data entry and junior copywriting jobs, according to The Wall Street Journal. Those tasks may be easier to automate. [...] But AI could also create opportunities. A Bloomberg article points to potential job growth in construction and manufacturing as companies build data centers and produce the chips that power the technology. Some higher-skilled office workers could also benefit if AI helps them become more productive. [...] The long-term impact on jobs remains unclear, but workers can take steps to prepare. Exploring AI chatbots, writing assistants and other tools may help people find ways to work more efficiently and develop skills that complement the technology.

items.summary: I understand the appeal. College is busy. Between classes, jobs, extracurriculars, leadership positions and trying to maintain some semblance of a social life, there are never enough hours in the day. AI makes things easier. [...] I am not asking anyone to abandon AI. I use it, and I recognize the benefits it provides. But I do think we need to become more conscientious about when we use it and what we are asking it to do for us. Let it help with the tedious tasks. Let it serve as a resource. But do not let it become a substitute for your own intellectual development. [...] There is also something to be said about individuality. items.summary: The bill’s advocates argue that its passage would serve as a rare bipartisan win and a victory for affordability. But critics, especially those on the left, are calling for Democrats to wait until the next Congress. “You just heard Americans demand much more of a say in a way that AI is shaping their lives,” says Michele Jawando, the CEO of Omidyar Network. “Whenever you try to ram something through in a lame duck Congress before you have a hundred new House members, that’s never a good look [...] Another major concern from critics is that the bill will lead to many more data centers getting built on federally-owned land. The Trump administration has embraced this idea, and signed an executive order in July 2025 directing the Interior and Energy departments to make federal sites available for data centers and to streamline their environmental reviews. “We’re going to ‘mine, baby, mine’ so we can ‘build, baby, build’ because we’ve got to build AI data centers,” Interior Secretary Doug [...] America’s data center boom has also been a gas boom. In the scramble to bring AI data centers online as fast as possible, many developers have built their own gas power plants instead of waiting to connect to the grid. Global Energy Monitor data reported by Wired show that U.S. gas projects powering data centers increased from roughly 4 gigawatts in early 2024 to 189 gigawatts in development by mid-2026. In some cases, these gas plants have worsened local pollution and exacerbated health issues

items.summary:
Cán bộ hướng dẫn công dân thao tác trên hệ thống dịch vụ công

Không chỉ hỗ trợ người dân hoàn thành thủ tục, cán bộ, chiến sĩ còn cố gắng sử dụng những cách giải thích đơn giản, dễ hiểu để người dân có thể tự thực hiện trong những lần tiếp theo. Đối với những người gặp khó khăn khi sử dụng công nghệ, cán bộ sẵn sàng hướng dẫn nhiều lần, giải đáp từng thắc mắc với thái độ tận tình, trách nhiệm. [...] Đối với những người thường xuyên sử dụng công nghệ, việc tạo tài khoản dịch vụ công, quét mã QR hoặc tải tài liệu đính kèm có thể thực hiện nhanh chóng. Tuy nhiên, với người cao tuổi và những người ít có điều kiện tiếp xúc với thiết bị điện tử, các thao tác này đôi khi gặp nhiều khó khăn.

Nhận thức được điều đó, cán bộ, chiến sĩ Công an xã Thuận An luôn chú trọng hướng dẫn cụ thể, kiên nhẫn giải thích từng bước để người dân hiểu và thực hiện đúng các thao tác cần thiết. [...] Những hoạt động hỗ trợ tuy giản dị nhưng mang ý nghĩa thiết thực, góp phần giúp người dân thuận lợi hơn trong giải quyết thủ tục hành chính, tiết kiệm thời gian, chi phí đi lại và từng bước nâng cao kỹ năng sử dụng dịch vụ công trực tuyến. Qua đó, Công an xã Thuận An tiếp tục đưa công nghệ đến gần hơn với người dân, nhất là những người còn gặp khó khăn trong tiếp cận công nghệ, để mọi người đều có cơ hội thụ hưởng những tiện ích của chuyển đổi số.

items.title: NVIDIA released a new RL framework:
items.summary:
NVIDIA released a new RL framework:

Your entire setup is one Python file:

- write a class with a step() function
- return a reward from it
- the framework handles the rest, up to 1T-class MoE training

In a typical RL framework, the environment and reward logic are added inside the trainer's codebase.

Adding a new task requires writing framework code, registering it, and wiring up config for it.

The reward usually comes from a separately trained reward model, which needs its own GPUs and placement next to the actor and critic.

NVIDIA's Molt framework drops both these requirements.

Every run takes an agent_path flag pointing to one Python module, and the trainer code never changes.

The module gives you two ways to plug in an agent.

> The first is an Env class where you write a step() function that receives the model's output and returns a reward, and the framework handles everything else, i.e., calling the model, tokenizing, and looping turn after turn until the episode ends.

> The second is a ChatAgent class, for agents that already exist as their own loop. Here, you write the loop yourself, calling the model through a standard OpenAI or Anthropic client, and the framework spins up a local server so those calls hit its vLLM engines instead of an external API.

Either way, the trainer sees the same thing, i.e., a trajectory of tokens and a reward at the end.

That reward can come from a string-match grader, code executed in a sandboxed subprocess, or an LLM-as-judge call.

So there is no reward model to train or place, and no environment code living inside the framework.

Under the hood, Molt runs a single trainable actor (plus an optional critic for PPO) on FSDP2, vLLM engines for rollout, and Ray queues between them, so generation, training, and weight sync overlap instead of running in lockstep.

Scaling just requires setting some flags on the same command.

The framework also splits the model across GPUs for you, so the script that trains an 8B model on one node can also train DeepSeek-V3-scale MoE models on a cluster by raising the parallelism flags.

Here's the repo: https://t.co/TafSfatER5

Since the framework is new, I am still experimenting with it and will share more about my learnings soon.

To dive deeper into how top AI labs are building RL Agents in 2026, I wrote a full article about it.

It covers the evolution from RLHF to GRPO with verifiable rewards and using an LLM-as-judge reward function. This idea extends RL training to non-verifiable agentic tasks without writing custom reward functions.

Read it below.

items.title: Claude Fable 5.2 leads scientific visual reasoning benchmark VIALS-AA; it makes more tool calls than any other Anthropic
items.summary:
Claude Fable 5.2 leads scientific visual reasoning benchmark VIALS-AA; it makes more tool calls than any other Anthropic model, unlike OpenAI models which make fewer as they get smarter

VIALS-AA is our implementation of @joinHandshakeAI’s VIALS benchmark for visual reasoning in life sciences research, across artifacts such as gel blots, plasmid maps, and phylogenies. Claude Fable 5.2 (max with fallback) scores 67% on VIALS-AA, ahead of Gemini 4 Carbon (high) at 64% and GPT-6 Astra (max) at 63%. Fable averages ~37 tool calls per task, while Astra averages ~8, the fewest of any model we’ve tested.

On turn 4 of this protein interaction task, Fable creates crops and asks to view them. On turn 10, it builds a color mask by thresholding color channels. On turn 17, it fits a circle to each arc and unrolls the arc into a straight strip. On turn 31, it counts the bars as peaks in an intensity profile. And on turn 41, it maps every detected spoke back on the original image to check its work. Fable batches calls on 28 of its 51 turns, averaging 1.75 tool calls per turn, compared with 1.12 for Sonnet 5.5.

items.title: Setting a new standard for responsible AI infrastructure | OpenAI
items.summary: The promise of AI is that it gives people more power to shape their own futures. It can help someone learn a new skill, build a business, or solve a problem that was previously out of reach. Building more computing infrastructure capacity in the United States can help lower the cost of delivering AI, put these tools in more people’s hands, and ensure America stays at the forefront of the technology. items.title: OpenAI gets $11 billion funding at $1.25 trillion valuation, source says | Reuters
items.summary:
Nov 6 (Reuters) - OpenAI has closed ‌on new funding of $11 billion, the initial part of a round ​that values the company ​at $1.25 trillion, a source familiar with ⁠the matter said on Friday.

The $11 ​billion raised so far represents ​only a portion of OpenAI's original target of up to $30 billion, while ​the company's valuation has ​come down from the $1.5 trillion level it ‌had ⁠initially sought, two investors said. items.title: OpenAI will keep investing in AI data centers despite election results, CFO tells CNBC
items.summary: OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar on Friday said the company will continue to invest in artificial intelligence infrastructure, even after voters strongly rebuked data centers during Tuesday's midterm elections.

items.title: OpenAI employees warned about operational security lapses for years, sources say | Reuters
items.summary:
OpenAI and Anthropic have tried to ​maintain a more open research culture to both ⁠attract employees and foster creativity that can lead to breakthroughs. The AI field is rooted in academia, where machine-learning scientists have openly discussed their research.

Some OpenAI employees are increasingly worried about this approach as AI grows more capable, according to the five people. [...] When asked about employees' concerns and their view that management did not act on these issues, OpenAI spokesperson Elana Widmann ​said that OpenAI is one of the most targeted organizations in the world. As a result, the company invests heavily in its security program to protect against attacks from insiders, cybercriminals and nation-states, she said. These workers argued that OpenAI's controls were so lax ‌that outsiders, including foreign governments, could obtain sensitive information about the AI lab's technology with relative ease, the people said.
